subject: Meadow Health pilot — temporary throughput entitlement & launch traffic plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Meadow Health pilot — temporary throughput entitlement & launch traffic plan

Team — looping you in early. Meadow Health (external) has a pilot launch on May 3rd and just shared a traffic forecast that spikes to ~1.8M tokens/day during the first 72 hours. They want a short-lived throughput uplift (temporary entitlement) to avoid client-side throttling.

Quick summary: 
- Ask: temporary rate uplift from their current trial quota to a transient entitlement for 10 days around launch (May 3–12).
- Forecast: see attached meadow_forecast_Q2_v1.xlsx — peak ingress 1.8M tokens/day, average 700k/day for the week; 6k concurrent requests at peak.
- Risks: burst causes tail latency increases on shared pools; product behavior around prefix caching + batching critical.
- Customer requests: SLA window (best-effort), a fallback model variant with lower memory footprint if capacity constrained, and a post-launch runbook for graceful degradation.

Primary asks for this thread: 
1) Product: are there any model-routing or prompt-routing constraints we need to set (tool-calls, structured output) that could increase per-request cost? Any recommended model variant for the fallback?
2) Infra/Ops (David): can we provision a transient entitlement or carve a soft capacity buffer in hosted pools? Approx cost estimate?
3) Response plan: who will be primary contact to approve/monitor the uplift during launch window?

I attached the initial entitlement request PDF and the forecast. I can set up a quick 30-min alignment if helpful — aiming to confirm by EOD Fri (Apr 23) to give us ~10 days runway.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-20T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meadow Health pilot — temporary throughput entitlement & launch traffic plan

Thanks Jordan — good context. A few product clarifications before we route to infra: 

- Model surface: which model family are they using for inference (large vs medium)? If they plan on long convo contexts or function calling, that materially affects kernel selection.
- Tokenization profile: do they expect many short requests (chat-like) or long docs (single prompts)? The forecast file is token-level but we need request-size distribution to tune batching.
- Fallback variant: For a rapid fallback we typically recommend a quantized-medium variant (cpu/quantized-gpu) that preserves semantics for prompt-completion but reduces memory pressure. Karthik — can you propose a specific model/quantization combo we can expose as the fallback?

If we can get answers to those 3 by EOD tomorrow I can prepare a short routing policy (latency-first for paid endpoints, fallback to quantized variant + reduced max_tokens) and a small intake PR that ops can use to provision.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. PM, Serving Platform
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-21T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meadow Health pilot — temporary throughput entitlement & launch traffic plan

Jordan / Marissa — we can support a temporary entitlement but need the following to estimate impact and set up monitoring: 

- Request-size distribution (avg tokens/request, p95 tokens/request) — affects concurrency and slot usage.
- Desired max RPS or tokens/s uplift (they gave daily tokens but not sustained RPS).
- Preferred region for traffic (us-west/us-east) — routing matters for capacity pools.

Operational notes: 
- We can carve a soft buffer in the hosted pool for 10 days; cost is roughly $X/day per 100k tokens/day of uplift (I will send exact numbers once I have RPS).
- We need a short runbook (attached draft runbook) with escalation points (oncall, eng triage, rollback trigger: sustained p99 > 2s or error rate > 1.5%).
- For a graceful downgrade we can automatically route to a quantized fallback model variant if health checks fail. That requires product to expose the fallback model name in the route config.

I'll slot in capacity contingent on the above. If we get RPS by EOD today I can commit a buffer and draft a monitoring dashboard.

-David
David Kim
Platform Reliability Lead
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-21T10:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meadow Health pilot — temporary throughput entitlement & launch traffic plan

Quick product suggestion: based on similar pilots, propose the following fallback pair: 
- Primary: open-llm-large-v2 (fp16) — default for quality-sensitive completions
- Fallback: open-llm-medium-q4 (4-bit quantized) — preserves <90% of completion fidelity in >2x token throughput efficiency

Config suggestions to expose in route: 
- fallback_model: open-llm-medium-q4
- max_tokens: reduce by 25% on fallback to protect tail latency
- batching: prefer continuous batching with max_batch_delay=8ms for chat-like traffic; increase to 20ms if many small requests to improve throughput.

I'll add a short PR with model names and suggested route flags by EOD.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Architect, Inference Runtime
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver@meadowhealth.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: eng@meadowhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-21T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meadow Health pilot — temporary throughput entitlement & launch traffic plan

Jordan / team — attaching our more granular request (meadow_forecast_Q2_v1.xlsx) and a short note on request profile. Some clarifications: 

- Model & traffic: We'll start on open-llm-large-v2; traffic is chat-like, average ~120 tokens/request, p95 ~820 tokens. Peak sustained RPS estimated at ~48 RPS over a 10-minute window during marketing-triggered flows.
- Region: prefer us-east for lower latency to our infra.
- SLA ask: they requested an SLA window for the pilot but are okay with best-effort for now — they mainly want predictability and an explicit fallback.

We can reduce token length on our side if needed; we prefer to rely on Redwood fallback rather than re-engineering prompts during the 10-day window. Let us know if you need a signed addendum for the temporary entitlement.

Thanks,
Oliver Hayes
Head of Integrations, Meadow Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, oliver@meadowhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-22T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meadow Health pilot — temporary throughput entitlement & launch traffic plan

Thanks all — summary and next steps: 

- Customer confirmed model (open-llm-large-v2), avg/p95 tokens and us-east region. (Oliver: thanks for the file.)
- Karthik to publish fallback model names + route flags (ETA: EOD today).
- David to provision a soft buffer in hosted us-east pool for May 3–12 pending final RPS numbers (David: please confirm provisioning and cost estimate in the monitoring doc).
- Marissa to prepare route config PR and default rollback triggers.
- Jordan will own day-of monitoring and be primary contact for Meadow; Soojin will be secondary.

If product/ops are aligned I will send the customer a short note confirming our plan + the sign-off required (signed addendum or email ok). Target: lock config by Apr 23 COB.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
